messages.content: Write a short scene in modern American English between two longtime adult friends. One of them has had a difficult day but is trying not to talk about it. Let the emotion come through naturally in dialogue, pauses, small actions, and what the character avoids saying. Do not directly explain the character's feelings to the reader. Keep the scene quiet and realistic.

“You want the last slice?”

“I'm not that hungry.”

Alex looked at the pizza box, then back at Jordan. “You ate two slices in the car.”

“That was different.”

“How?”

Jordan shrugged. “Car calories don't count.”

Alex smiled, but Jordan had already reached for her drink instead. She turned the straw around between her fingers, watching the ice knock against the sides of the cup.

“You sure you're okay?” Alex asked.

“Yep.”

“That was fast.”

“What was fast?”

“The most convincing ‘yep’ I've ever heard.”

Jordan gave her a look. “I'm doing great.”

“Right.”

A few seconds passed.

Jordan picked up the pizza slice and set it back down. “Can we not tonight?”

Alex nodded. “Yeah.”

She slid the plate a little closer anyway.

Jordan glanced at it.

“I said I wasn't hungry.”

“I know.”

“Then why'd you move it?”

“Because you're going to change your mind in approximately thirty seconds.”

Jordan almost smiled. “You sound very confident.”

“I've known you too long.”

That got a real laugh out of her, small and tired but real.

“Thirty seconds?” Jordan asked.

“Twenty-five.”

Jordan picked up the slice.

“See?” Alex said.

“Shut up.”

Alex grinned. “There you are.””
